nm_west_side_lost_cam_area_3_5.blurb: A tall sandstone wall at the village of Waterflow, a short drive from Farmington in the northwest of the state. Eleven lines, nearly all traditional with fixed anchors on most, plus a pair of A2 aid routes. Free climbing runs from an easy 5.6 through a solid cluster of 5.10s, with a couple of 5.11s at the top end. Expect to place your own gear and to be comfortable on a real wall; it is not a gentle spot for a first outdoor day, and a nearby canyon is the friendlier choice for beginners.
nm_west_side_lost_cam_area_3_5.parking_note: Coming from Farmington, drive through the first stoplight in Waterflow, turn right, and go roughly a tenth of a mile to a dirt road on the right. Pull off to one side so the road stays clear.

nm_big_horn_wall.blurb: The signature wall at Sitting Bull Falls, southwest of Carlsbad: ten sport lines on very good limestone that rank among the hardest in the state. Grades start around 5.10 but the core is 5.12, with a few 5.13s and one 5.14. Steep, sustained and pumpy, with big holds and long reaches. The wall faces north and gets almost no direct sun, so it is shady and crowds are thin; it is a cold place in winter and best suited to climbers who already lead the harder grades.
nm_big_horn_wall.parking_note: Leave the car in the day-use lot at the falls. The wall can be seen from there but is a good deal farther than it looks.
nm_big_horn_wall.approach: Take the paved path toward the falls for about 30 yards, then the signed dirt trail up to the top of the waterfall. Follow the steep switchbacking path until it eases off, then bear right onto a faint climbers' trail heading west. Drop down to the base of the neighbouring Rose Bud Wall and walk west along its foot to reach the Big Horn Wall.

nm_03_wall_of_dreams.blurb: A short wall on the New Side of Mentmore, the sandstone climbing area outside Gallup. It holds several of the harder lines on this side: seven sport routes and a few gear or top-rope lines, running from an easy-to-moderate 5.9 crack through a bunch of 5.10s and a strong run of 5.11s, topped by one 5.12. Cliffs at Mentmore are generally 25 to 50 feet tall. The wall catches sun in the afternoon, so it suits cooler days. Sandstone here weakens when wet, so give it time to dry after rain.
nm_03_wall_of_dreams.parking_note: Take Mentmore Road about a mile and a half, up and over the rise, to the climbers' parking lot.
nm_03_wall_of_dreams.approach: From the lot it is about a five-minute walk south to the New Side cliffs.

nm_snake_den.blurb: A small cluster of ten boulder problems beside the Sugarloaf trail in the Aguirre Springs area, on the east side of the Organ Mountains outside Las Cruces. The two main blocks are the namesake boulder and a big wave-shaped block a short way north. Problems stretch from easy V0 up to a single V7, but most sit between V0 and V3, with a pair of harder lines, so it is a fine stop for an easy to middling session. The hillside setting is scenic and rattlesnakes are a real possibility, so watch where you step.
nm_snake_den.parking_note: Use the group-site parking in the Aguirre Springs recreation area, on the east side of the Organ Mountains.
nm_snake_den.approach: From the group-site lot, follow the Sugarloaf trail uphill across the slabs. The boulders sit alongside the trail as it gains height.

nm_sugarloaf.blurb: A big granite dome rising on the eastern flank of the Organ Mountains above Las Cruces, the largest formation in the range. Eleven traditional lines, many of them multi-pitch and among the longest in the Organs. Most are moderate, around 5.6 to 5.8, with a few 5.10s and 5.11s. The rock is good overall but holds some loose blocks, so test holds before trusting them. The setting is remote, routes stay shady for much of the day and the wind can blow. Carry enough kit to handle being caught out.
nm_sugarloaf.parking_note: Park at the Aguirre Springs campground on the east side of the Organ Mountains and start from there.
